svg.title: Combinatorial BPE vs standard BPE on 11 languages
svg.desc: 32% fewer tokens and 4.1% lower bits per byte overall, better on all 11 sources.

text.font-family: -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, 'Noto Sans CJK SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif

svg.text: One tokenizer, one model, 11 languages: Combinatorial vs standard BPE

text.font-family: -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, 'Noto Sans CJK SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif

svg.text: Same 32,768 embedding rows, same 8-layer GPT (RoPE, SwiGLU, QK-norm, Muon), same compute (22,500 steps × 16k tokens),

text.font-family: -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, 'Noto Sans CJK SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif

svg.text: trained on Wikipedia in 6 languages + GitHub code in 5 languages.

text.font-family: -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, 'Noto Sans CJK SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif

svg.text: Fewer tokens for the same text

svg.text: Bits per byte on held-out text is tokenizer-independent; standard BPE = byte-level BPE with GPT-2 pretokenization trained on the same data (the stronger of two baselines).

text.font-family: -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, 'Noto Sans CJK SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif

svg.text: Combinatorial BPE is also better at equal data (-0.5%) and on every source; with an older GPT-2-style recipe the overall gain is 3.7%.

text.font-family: -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, 'Noto Sans CJK SC', 'Microsoft YaHei', sans-serif

svg.text: Single seed per model, 42–45M parameters, learning rate tuned for each tokenizer.
